title: Range Buff

==Description==
The '''Range Buff''' is a buff that increases a tower's range. It is shown on the tower with a blue icon of multiple waves.

==Mechanics==
'''Range Buff''' range reduction is calculated as:
::<big>'''Range × (1 + Range Buff)'''</big>
:::where '''Range Buff''' is the buff supplied in decimal form (for example, 10% is 0.1).

The range of a tower affected by the '''Range Buff''' can be in decimal form, instead of being rounded down or rounded up to the nearest interger. For example, a tower with 5 range with a 50% '''Range Buff''' will have a range of 7.5.

The following towers are either partially or fully not affected by the '''Range Buff''':
*All [[units]].
*The [[Shotgunner]], as its bullets do not extend into the increased range.
*The [[DJ Booth]] cannot have its range boosted by another [[DJ Booth]].
**Other range buff sources, like the [[Ranger]], can still apply it.
*Circling range of the [[Pursuit]] and [[Ace Pilot]].
**The radius in which towers gain hidden detection from the [[Ace Pilot]] also cannot be increased.
**These towers' attack range can still be increased.
*The sentry building range of the [[Engineer]].
*The deadzone ranges of towers like the [[Biologist]] and [[Engineer]].
**The attack range for these towers can still be increased.
*Secondary orange range of towers like the range buff range for the [[Ranger]] or the gravestone range for the [[Necromancer]].
**The main range of these towers can still be increased.
*The chain range of the [[Electroshocker]].
**The attack range can still be increased.
*The explosion radius from [[Splash Damage|Splash Damage towers]] cannot be increased.

==Applied By==
The following towers or consumables can apply the '''Range Buff''' to other towers:
*[[DJ Booth]] (Passive)
*[[Ranger]] (Passive for 20 seconds at the beginning of each wave)
*[[Range Flag]] (Passive)
*[[UAV]] (Passive)
*[[Easter Egg]] (Passive for 20 seconds)
The following event features can apply the '''Range Buff''' to towers:

* [[The Moon]] (Passive, [[Null & Void Event|Null & Void]])

The following towers used to have the '''Range Buff''':
*{{Color|Golden}} [[Pyromancer]] (Passive)
*{{Color|Golden}} [[Cowboy]] (Passive)
*[[Slasher]] (Old ''Knife Throw'' ability)

The following removed towers had the '''Range Buff''':
*{{Color|Platinum}} [[Pyromancer]] (Passive)

title: Damage Indicators
wikitext_excerpt:
==Description==
'''Damage Indicators''' are numbers that pop up on enemies when a tower is selected. These numbers are how much damage was dealt to the enemy. The colors used by them mainly varies based on the damage type of the tower or unit. As not all damage types are registered by the game, not all sources of damage will have them appear.
__TOC__

==Regular Indicators==
[[File:RegularIndicator.png|100px|thumb]]
Regular indicators are the basic indicator that appears on most towers. These indicators are colored red. If a tower does not fall into any of the categories below, it uses these indicators.
{{Clear}}

==Explosion Indicators==
[[File:ExplosionIndicator.png|100px|thumb]]
Explosion indicators appear when a tower or unit deals explosion damage. They are also appear when a tower deals burn damage. These indicators are colored orange. Additionally, damage under this type will bypass defense. These following towers and units deal this type of damage:
*[[Demoman]]
*[[Ace Pilot]]
*[[Military Base]]
*[[Tank]]
*[[Railgun Tank]]
*[[Rocketeer]]
*[[Trapper]]
*[[Pyromancer]]
*[[Tesla]]
*[[Necromancer]]
*[[Archer]]
*[[Commando]]
*[[Firework Technician]]
*[[Jester]]
*[[Snowballer]]
*[[Swarmer]]
*[[Missile APC]]
*[[Grenadier]]
*[[War Machine Sentry]]
*[[Bomber Elf (Unit)|Bomber Elf]]
*[[Gift Bomber]]
*[[Ripped Elf (Unit)|Ripped Elf]]

However, despite this, not every single explosive actually uses these indicators. The following towers do not use explosive indicators, meaning they do not bypass defense:
*[[Paintballer]]
**Uses Regular indicators.
*[[Slime Trooper]]
**Uses Regular indicators.
*[[Hallow Punk]]
**Uses Regular indicators.
*[[Ivy]]
**Uses Energy indicators.

Additionally, the [[Elementalist]] uses similarly colored damage indicators for its burn related attacks, though it shares no other traits with explosion indicators, such as defense bypass.

==Collision Indicators==
[[File:CollisionIndicator.png|100px|thumb]]
Collision indicators appear when a tower or unit deals unit collision damage. This means it has a few traits, such as bypassing defense, damaging [[Lead (Attribute)|Lead]] enemies, bypassing [[Tank (Attribute)|Tank]]  and dealing no damage to [[Ghost (Attribute)|Ghost]] enemies. These indicators are colored yellow. This means it will mainly appear when a unit collides with another enemy. There is one exception to this, as the [[Trapper]]'s spike and bear traps deal unit collision damage, making them use these indicators.

==Melee Indicators==
[[File:MeleeIndicators.png|100px|thumb]]
Melee indicators appear when a tower or unit deals melee damage. These indicators are yellow. These indicators are quite inconsistent, as multiple towers that would be considered melee are not registered as ones. These following towers and units deal this type of damage:
*[[Gladiator]]
*[[Warden]]
*[[Sledger]]
*[[Executioner]]
*[[Riot Guard]]
*[[Slasher]]
**With its main attack.
*[[Assassin]]
*[[Warlock]]
**With its melee attack.
*[[Brawler]]
These towers, despite looking like they would deal such damage, do not have melee indicators:
*[[Sword Skeleton]] and [[Skeleton Knight]].
**Both use regular indicators.
*[[Executioner Skeleton]].
**Despite [[Executioner]] having melee indicators, [[Executioner Skeleton]] does not. It has regular indicators.
*[[Guardian Elf]]
**Uses regular indicators.

==Poison Indicators==
[[File:PoisonIndicator.png|100px|thumb]]
Poison indicators appear when a tower deals poison damage. These indicators are colored green. These following towers and units deal this type of damage:
*[[Toxic Gunner]]
*[[Saboteur]]
*[[Ivy]]
*[[Jester]]

The [[Swarmer]]'s sting damage used to have its damage create such indicators, though this is not longer the case starting from [[v1.63.0]].

==Chillness Indicators==

title: Firerate Bug
wikitext_excerpt:
{{Removed|date = 6th of June 2026}}
{{Improve|this page and majority of tower/unit pages require updating}}
The '''Firerate Bug''', also known as the '''RoF (Rate of Fire) Bug''', was a bug that slightly increased the firerate of all towers and units. This increase was not displayed on the statistics in the game. This bug significantly affected the statistics of fast-firing towers, such as the [[Minigunner]] and [[Ace Pilot]], by significantly decreasing their DPS, whereas slow-firing towers like the [[Ranger]] or [[Sniper]] were hardly affected.

This has been fixed as of the 6th of June 2026, and all firerate statistics in the game are considered to be accurate unless affected by a different unrelated bug.

{{RightTOC}}

==Prior to 5th of June 2026==
The '''Firerate Bug''' affects all towers and units that can directly attack enemies, meaning the only towers that are not affected are the [[Farm]], [[Medic]] and the [[Firework Technician]] and the only units that are not affected are the [[Humvee]], [[Humvee 2]], [[Elf]], [[Bomber Elf (Unit)|Bomber Elf]], [[Skeleton (Unit)|Skeleton]], [[Giant Skeleton (Unit)|Giant Skeleton]] and [[Hallow Guard (Unit)|Hallow Guard]]. The '''Firerate Bug''' does not affect the firerate of some secondary attacks towers or units may perform, some damage-over-time effects applied by towers (like burn from the [[Pyromancer]]) or certain other cooldowns.

The '''Firerate Bug''' increases the firerate of a tower/unit depending on its firerate, which can vary anywhere between 0.017 and 0.032 seconds. The firerate increase affects fast firing towers the most; for example, the [[Minigunner]] at Level 4 should have a firerate of 0.09, but because of the '''Firerate Bug''', it has a firerate of about 0.117, decreasing its DPS from 166.67 to 128.20, which is a decrease of 38.47 DPS, or a loss of about 23.08 DPS. Meanwhile, slow firing towers are barely affected by it; for example, the [[Ranger]] at Level 4 should have a firerate of 8, but because of the '''Firerate Bug''', it has a firerate of about 8.025, decreasing its DPS from 156.26 to 155.76, which is a decrease of 0.30 DPS, or a loss of 0.2% DPS.

The [[Firerate Buff]] is also affected by the '''Firerate Bug''', making it less effective. For example, the Level 4 [[Minigunner]] without the '''Firerate Bug''' with a 50% firerate boost should have a firerate of 0.06, but with the '''Firerate Bug''' it has a firerate of 0.083. This means that its DPS with a 50% firerate boost is decreased from 250 to 180.72, which is a decrease of 69.28 DPS, or a loss of 27.71% DPS.

On this Wiki, the firerate statistic of all towers and units is increased by specific values based on the firerate. While technically possible to calculate by hand, due to the effort it would take, it is overall recommended to either use [[Help:Neowtext#ROFBUG|Neowtext]] or [https://fiheron.github.io/dps-calc/ an online calculator].

==Prior to the 9th of January 2023==
Prior to the 9th of January 2023, the firerate increase caused by the '''Firerate Bug''' for units was higher than it currently is. The firerate increase was generally around 0.03 seconds. For towers, the firerate increase remained at around 0.008 seconds.

On this Wiki, the firerate statistic of all towers and units after the [[V1.6.0|Violent Night Update]] and before the 9th of January 2023 is increased by 0.008 and 0.03 respectively, unless stated otherwise. This does not, however, mean the actual value is this; it can vary between towers and even between matches.

==Prior to the Violent Night Update==
Prior to the [[V1.6.0|Violent Night Update]], the firerate increase caused by the '''Firerate Bug''' for units was lower than it was before the [[V1.6.0|Violent Night Update]]. The firerate increases could be anywhere between 0.008 and 0.017 seconds, but the increase was generally around 0.008 seconds. This is the same as the current situation.

title: Leaderboard
wikitext_excerpt:
'''Leaderboard''' ---- '''Leaderboard''' is a feature that displays current global rankings of various statistics in the game lobbies.
==Lobby Leaderboards== [[File:LobbyLeaderboard.png|300px|thumb]] In the [[Main Lobby]], two boards can be found on the sides of the [[Elevators]] are, which are the '''Leaderboards''' for this part of the game. These display the current month's total statistics for up to 50 players. Their avatar icon, username, level and total statistic are displayed next to their spot on the '''Leaderboard'''. Top three players are displayed on podiums next to the '''Leaderboards'''. The first '''Leaderboard''' is total triumphs. This displays the total triumphs in [[Frost Mode|Frost]] or [[Fallen Mode|Fallen]] for players this month. The second '''Leaderboard''' is total {{Exp|}}. This display total {{Exp|}} for players this month. Any players in the top three of either two '''Leaderboards''' obtain the [[Champion Nametag]] through their [[Gift Box]], which they will get to keep even after the month ends. ==Intermission Lobby Leaderboards== [[File:IntermissionLobbyLeaderboard.png|300px|thumb]] In both the [[Survival Intermission Lobby|Survival]] and [[Hardcore Intermission Lobby|Hardcore Intermission Lobbies]], two large signs can be found displaying the '''Leaderboards'''. These show the top triumphs for the current month and day, respective to the mode of the lobby: *'''Survival Lobby''': Tracks triumphs in [[Easy Mode|Easy]], [[Casual Mode|Casual]], [[Intermediate Mode|Intermediate]], [[Molten Mode|Molten]], [[Fallen Mode|Fallen]] and [[Frost Mode|Frost]] modes. *'''Hardcore Lobby''': Tracks triumphs exclusively in [[Hardcore Mode|Hardcore]]. Unlike other '''Leaderboards''', however, no additional rewards are granted for placing in the top three or achieving first place. ==Trivia== *[[Tutorial]] triumphs used to count for the '''Top Triumphs''' leaderboard. {{BrowseNavBox}}

==Description==
'''Tower Defense Simulator''' ('''TDS'''), is a game created by [[Paradoxum Games]] on the 5th of June 2019, though it was not officially released until the 14th of June 2019. It is a tower defense game where players are tasked with defending the exit from hordes of enemies using towers. It is playable on PC, mobile and consoles.

'''Tower Defense Simulator''' was [[Tower Defense Simulator Award Nominations|nominated for awards]] multiple times in the Bloxies and the Innovation Awards, though it only won the 8th Annual Bloxy Awards in the ''Best Game Trailer'' category.

'''Tower Defense Simulator''' has various social media accounts, including an [https://x.com/paradoxum_games X account], a [https://discord.gg/tds Discord server], [https://www.youtube.com/@ParadoxumGames YouTube channel] and [https://www.reddit.com/r/TDS_Roblox/ Reddit subreddit]. Other accounts also exist, though they are tied to [[Paradoxum Games]] rather than '''Tower Defense Simulator''' specifically, meaning content from [[Paradoxum Games]]' other games also appear there.

==Gameplay==
The main gameplay loop of '''Tower Defense Simulator''' revolves around the players using their [[towers]] and [[consumables]] to defend a map they have chosen from [[enemies]]. Players can pick a limited number of towers and consumables into their loadout. These have varying abilities making them excel in different areas, like some towers being better suited for the early waves or certain towers being used to provide buffs to other towers.

Players can pick a [[Maps|map]] of their choosing in either the main lobby or the intermission lobby. The main lobby allows for picking maps via [[Elevators]], while intermission lobby allows for players to vote on which map they want to play on. In certain modes, like the special maps or [[Challenge Trials]], there is a set map which cannot be changed.

The mode can also be chosen by players. If a map is accessed through the main lobby, there is a vote between the survival modes, while for [[Hardcore Mode|Hardcore]] mode, no such vote is held due to it only having one. If a map is chosen in the intermission lobby, there is no mode vote as it was already chosen through the [[Matchmaking]] menu by the player.

When a match starts, hordes of enemies will be sent out. Initially, these enemies do not possess any abilities and they will simply walk towards the exit. However, as the match goes on, these enemies will receive various abilities or attributes, such as immunities, abilities to support other enemies and attacks which stun or debuff towers. On the final wave, a major boss will spawn, which the player needs to defeat to triumph the match.

'''Tower Defense Simulator''' also offers [[PVP]], where instead of surviving all the waves, the players are tasked with defeating another player by surviving for longer. [[PVP]] has its own unique mechanics, unique statistics of towers for the mode and consumables that are only usable in [[PVP]] mode.

After beating a match, players are rewarded with various currency, such as {{Coins|Coins}}, {{Exp|}} and {{Gem|Gems}}. These are mainly used to progress through the game, as they allow the player to unlock new areas of the game, purchase items and obtain [[cosmetics]].

'''Tower Defense Simulator Award Nominations''' ---- Every year, Roblox hosts the Innovation Awards event (formerly the Bloxys). Tower Defense Simulator has been nominated by Roblox in the Bloxys and Innovation Awards five times, all in different categories, winning only one of them.
__TOC__ ==Roblox Innovation Awards 2026 (Voting ongoing)== In the [[w:c:Roblox:Roblox Innovation Awards 2026|Roblox Innovation Awards 2026]], Tower Defense Simulator was nominated for ''Best Strategy Experience''. The reward was originally listed by BelowNatural as a Bloxy skin of community's choice, though it was quickly changed to just a special celebration. A KJ [[Brawler]] skin was also shown off by a developer at one point, though its lack of acknowledgement points towards it being a joke and not an actual reward. ===Nominees=== {| class="article-table pad-5 align-center" style="width:350px;" !Game !Result |- |{{RLinkG|131346454575416|Mini War}} | class="neutral-table" |Nominated |- |{{RLinkG|9503261072|Tower Defense X}} | class="neutral-table" |Nominated |- |{{RLinkG|3260590327|Tower Defense Simulator}} | class="neutral-table" |Nominated |- |{{RLinkG|2569453732|Rise of Nations}} | class="neutral-table" |Nominated |} ===Gallery=== {{Gallery|Open = Yes| InnovationAwards2026Icon.png|Icon for the Innovation Awards. title: Tower Defense Simulator Toys
wikitext_excerpt:
'''Toys''' ---- ''For information about Merchandise, click [[Merchandise|here]].'' There are various Tower Defense Simulator-themed Toys, generally sold by Paradoxum Games though also occasionally sold by others, which can be mini-figures or plushies. They are based on multiple things that appear in the game, such as towers, enemies or units. Toys sold by Paradoxum Games can be found at the [https://shop.paradoxum.games/ Paradoxum Games website] or through their Merch Shop. Toys sold by Paradoxum Games come with additional in-game rewards, usually skins. These can '''only be gotten through the in-game Merch Shop'''. Purchases on the [https://shop.paradoxum.games/ Paradoxum Games website] will not come with any rewards. title: Tower Defense Simulator UGC
wikitext_excerpt:
'''Tower Defense Simulator UGC''' ---- Tower Defense Simulator has '''user-generated content (UGC)''' made themed around it that can be bought in the Roblox marketplace. These are generally made by the Paradoxum Games group, though there were some made by the clothing designers from the Tower Defense Simulator Discord that can be worn alongside the shirt and pants. BelowNatural has also uploaded a few accessories on his account. This page does not include any accessories made by Roblox, regardless of whether they were obtainable in Tower Defense Simulator or are themed around it.
__TOC__ ==Paradoxum Games== The [[Paradoxum Games]] group released multiple UGC themed items around Tower Defense Simulator as part of updates. While they were mostly items with limited stock, some were made purchasable permanently. ===General=== These were released without any in-game event tied to them. {| class="empty-table pad-5 align-center" style="width:300px; margin:0 auto" |[[File:BaseballMortarCapOfficial.png|175px]] |[[File:BaseballMortarBackpackOfficial.png|175px]] |[[File:FallenEngineerWingsBelow.png|175px]] |[[File:FallenEngineerHairBelow.png|175px]] |- |{{RLinkC|133999213531013|Baseball Mortar's Cap (OFFICIAL)}} |{{RLinkC|117936505339965|Baseball Mortar's Backpack (OFFICIAL)}} |{{RLinkC|82979124228483|Fallen Engineer's Wings}} |{{RLinkC|74037952317708|Fallen Engineer's Hair}} |- |[[File:FrostBlasterBackpackOfficial.png|175px]] |[[File:FrostBlasterHelmetOfficial.png|175px]] |[[File:ScoutVestBelow.png|175px]] |[[File:ScoutHeadwearBelow.png|175px]] |- |{{RLinkC|122870584870737|Frost Blaster's Backpack (OFFICIAL)}} |{{RLinkC|78223623799015|Frost Blaster's Helmet (OFFICIAL)}} |{{RLinkC|116099329550896|Scout Vest (OFFICIAL)}} |{{RLinkC|86590017904678|Scout Headwear (OFFICIAL)}} |} ===The Hunt Event=== As part of [[The Hunt Event]], an accessory was released which could have been obtained from the [[Quests#After The Hunt|After The Hunt]] quest.
